correctness.rationale: Kameoka's primary PDF defines the same convex body through the sinh kinetic symbol and its support Finsler metric. At fixed Euclidean radius r, expanding q(xi)=2 sum(cosh xi_j-1) into positive even powers and applying the sharp power-sum bounds d^(1-m)r^(2m)<=sum_j xi_j^(2m)<=r^(2m) gives exact minimum and maximum q on the sphere. Inverting q=|E| gives the inner/outer Euclidean radii; support-function inclusions give the norm bounds, and strict equality cases of the power sums give the axis/diagonal classification. Independent numerical replay checked both boundary radii for d=2..7 and five energies.
risks: The result compares the constant-energy support norm to Euclidean distance; it does not assert that arbitrary potentials realize every extremal rate.
